author: Andrea Verschuyl
title: This Hidden Massachusetts Park Blends Art and Nature - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrea Verschuyl ,
9 hours ago
Looking for ways to enjoy a day outdoors? Why not head to the most unique park in Massachusetts? The deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum in Lincoln combines stunning scenery with inspiring sculptures, making it the state’s only spot where visitors can break in their walking shoes while brushing up on their art theory.
Why deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum Stands Out Kristin Shoemaker via Flickr Mark this incredibly unique park as one of the most underrated Massachusetts attractions . The deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum, is perched above the shore of idyllic Flints Pond and the lovely Flints Pond Trail and is just 30 minutes from big-city Boston. If you’re looking to get out of town, it’s an excellent day trip destination, offering hundreds of artworks and 30 acres of trails for an affordable admission price.
The Sculpture Park is open year-round (hours change seasonally), and, at any given time, you’ll find more than 50 outdoor sculptures on display in the Massachusetts sculpture park. If you want something to do outside on a beautiful day, plan a visit. The gorgeous property offers everything from hikes to art to family-friendly activities.
James O’Keefe via Flickr The property once belonged to Julian and Elizabeth de Cordova, who were both passionate about art and travel. The property was left to the town of Lincoln in 1930 with the stipulation that it would become a public museum of art. The deCordova opened in 1950 and remains the largest park of its kind in New England.
The deCordova also hosts art-themed summer camps and other community events.
What You’ll See and Do at the deCordova Terry Donovan via Flickr Since its debut, improvements have been made to deCordova in fits and spurts. Landscape architects designed the grounds to enhance the permanent sculptures, carefully considering the intentions of each exhibit and mirroring them in the scenery.
While the Museum’s indoor galleries are currently closed for renovations, the sculpture park, café, and retail store are open to visitors.
Take your time at deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum. Every artwork expresses something different, depending on the season, time of day, and weather. The sculptures are worth viewing from all angles, inviting consideration of their meaning and relationship to space.
What to Know Before You Go Laura Bernhardt via Flickr Address
51 Sandy Pond Road, Lincoln, MA 01773
781-259-8355
Website via Trustees
Hours
Summer: Tuesday – Sunday
Winter: Wednesday – Sundays
Visit the website for specific seasonal hours.
Do note: The indoor galleries are closed for renovations.
Admission
FREE: Lincoln residents, children 12 and under, Trustees members, and, with supporting documentation, visitors with EBT, WIC, Mass Health, and METCO students and their families
$14: Adults
$12: Seniors
$12: Students
Accessibility
Visit the Facilities & Accessibility section of the website for information.
For latest news and information, follow deCordova’s Facebook or Instagram .
DeCordova is also just a stone’s throw from Boston, making it a convenient outing for those unwilling to waste hours in traffic. Make your plans to visit the most unique park in Massachusetts this season.
